author: Mark Twain (Samuel L. Clemens)
title: Life on the Mississippi
edition: Boston: James R. Osgood and Company, 1883, with more than 300 illustrations, as shown by the photographed title page in Project Gutenberg eBook245 HTML (https://www.gutenberg.org/files/245/245-h/images/titlepage.jpg). Original English prose transcription; line wrapping is joined within paragraphs. Original paragraph boundaries, dialect, punctuation, underscore emphasis and transcribed footnotes are retained. Twain’s own footnotes, which Project Gutenberg sets inline in bracketed markup, are given in Project Gutenberg’s note form: the citing word carries “[1]” (“[2]” for a second note in the same paragraph), and the note follows that paragraph as its own block, “[Footnote 1: …]”. No modern introduction or digitizer boilerplate is included. The library text runs from the prefatory extract “The ‘Body of the Nation’” through Chapters 1–60 and Appendices A–D; the table of contents is omitted. A note with no citing word in the transcription (Chapter 40, “Illustrations of it thoughtlessly omitted by the advertiser”, which the file sets as its own paragraph) follows the paragraph before it with no anchor, as “[Footnote 1: …]” opened in its first paragraph and closed at the end of its last, its own paragraphs kept. The passages read by the Grade 11 calendar readings (blocks 15–24, 27–46 and 49–166: the end of Chapter 1 and Chapters 2–3) were compared word by word, punctuation and capitals included, with the OCR text of two copies of the Osgood printing (Internet Archive lifeonmississipp00twai_0 and cu31924022606317) and, where they differed, the page images. The transcription is not a close copy of that printing: it sets the printing’s double quotation marks as single ones and its inner single ones as double, closes up most of its spaced contractions (“it ’s”, “war n’t”), leaves some of its italics unmarked (“now”, “your”, “was” and “then” in blocks 69, 87, 92 and 133) and runs the song in blocks 58–59 together as prose; these conventions are left as transcribed. Its single quotation marks and the readings “raftman’s” and “chucks” match the London edition (Chatto & Windus, 1883; Internet Archive lifeonmississip01twaigoog), though its American spellings do not, so its exemplar remains unidentified. In these passages sixty-three readings changed to the Osgood text. Spelling: “Shakspeare” (blocks 19 and 21), “travelled” (28), “ploughed” (39), “sceptre” (46), “mouldy” (77), “marvellous” (166). Words: “the classifying” (18), “salvages” (28, in “explain hell to the salvages”), “twyste as” (58, run together in the transcription), “rilay - - - e,” (59, where it had “rilay--”), “lam” (60), “sufferins” (63), “they was sneaks” (72), “raftsman’s”, “better then Ohio water” (74), “shucks” (76), “it was a bar’l” (92), “hanted” (96). Capitals: “sans peur et sans reproche” (18), “whoo-oop!” (66). Punctuation: “Louis XIV. of” (27), “river occurred” (42), “Gulf;” (43), “chief’s” (43), “Then, for” (52), “listen,--” (56), the closing quotation mark after the song (59), “three times before” (67), “lightning and purr” (68), “played, and” (73), “ways;” (74), a colon before the dash in “says:--”, “out:--” and “this:--” (blocks 61, 64, 67, 70, 75, 77, 131, 135 and 146) and in “I just says:” (143, where the dash is not printed), a comma in “says,--” (blocks 78, 80, 81, 82, 84, 87, 90, 92, 93, 94 and 95), “bend?” (79), “why?” (80), “alone,--”, “usual,--” and “together,--” (100), “go,--” (101), “Yes sir,” (106), “dead?” (109), “lightning?” (118), “Good!” (134), “are you?” (142) and “Yes, sir, it’s” (152). The printing’s footnote to “lagniappe” in block 21 (“See page 450.”) is absent from the transcription and is not restored here. The passages read by the Grade 11 school nights (blocks 5–14, 169–175, 193–238, 260–286, 289–308, 326–336, 348–375, 378–407, 498–501, 509–538, 578–582, 603–610 and 639–645; blocks 169–172, 289–308, 326–336 and 378–407 are also the text of the four nights that keep their own wording) were then collated the same way, and the chapter headings between collated passages (blocks 25–26, 47–48, 167–168, 287–288 and 376–377) were checked against the printing, which sets them as “CHAPTER II.” over a title in capitals; the headings keep the arabic numeral and title case. Every collated passage, the calendar passages included, was also compared for word division and hyphenation, which the first comparison had left out; a hyphen at the end of a printed line is ambiguous, and there the transcription stands. This changed 102 further places to the Osgood text, and the printing’s misprint “beeen” (block 374) is kept. Spelling: “youthfulest” (9), “centre” (172), “marvellous” (284, and twice in 499), “gayly” (351), “sombre” (373), “villanous” (378), “vice” (501), “travelled” (641), “Oölitic” (645). Words: “all glass” (172), “lost so much time getting her off that it was plain the darkness” (260), “stern marks” (351), “sparklingly” (372), “becomes” (500), “once again” (521), “a shortening” (641). Capitals and emphasis: “old Mississippi River which La Salle” (12), “_Now_,” (282, where the transcription had capitals). Punctuation: “Gulf’s” (13), “Hannibal, Missouri.” (170), “‘gingerbread,’” and “gauge-cocks;” (172), “stage.” (210), “Well yonder’s” (263), four points after each call in block 266, the closing quotation mark before the dash in “Quarter-less’--”, “Seven-and’--”, “Six-and’--” and “crossing and’--” (266, 277, 281, 349), “such as:” (267, where no dash follows), the closing quotation mark after “now.” (306), “followed still” (351), “consuming,” (359), “No, sir,” (361), “apart.’” (371), “in it, painted” (372), “a month and” (581), “per cent of” (582), no quotation mark after “Period,” (645), question marks in blocks 199, 295, 304, 374, 375, 382, 397 and 580, a colon before the dash (“said:--” and the like) in blocks 196, 200, 233, 235, 263, 269, 272, 278, 285, 289, 328, 330, 348, 351, 523, 533 and 603, and a comma before it in blocks 238 (twice), 262, 292, 305, 326, 333, 351 (twice), 355, 380, 384, 511, 518, 521 and 531. Word division: “canebrakes” (36), “up-stream” (52), “three quarters” (74, 331, 382, 645), “deck-hand” (172, 173), “bar-keeper” (174), “day-dreams” (175), “memorandum-book” (234), “a while” (238), “pilot-house” (261), “W---- stepped” (262), “steamboat” (284), “sycamore snag” (306), “down-stream” (326), “every one” (332), “re-perusal” (372), “forever” (378), “toothpick” (380), “drift-wood” (397), “nine tenths” (511, 582), “two-hundred-mile” (639). The conventions named above hold in these passages too; there the transcription also leaves unmarked the italics of “only” (263), “exactly” and “George!” (270), “Six” (281), “I” (361), “starts” (397), “him” (500) and “after” (607), and writes “Caesar’s” (228) for the printed ligature “Cæsar’s”. The printing begins a new paragraph at “I can’t tell.” within block 384; the break is not restored, so that the block numbering stands. scope.collated lists the collated text, blocks 5–175, 193–238, 260–308, 326–336, 348–407, 498–501, 509–538, 578–582, 603–610 and 639–645; the rest of the work follows the transcription uncollated.

rights.basis: The associated photographed title page identifies this as the Boston Osgood1883 printing, outside the US copyright term in2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly identifies eBook245 as public domain in the USA. The dated title-page image was visually checked on2026-10-07.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (pglaf mirror of ebook 245). Removed the Gutenberg header, footer, licence, producer credit and table of contents; replaced each of the transcription’s inline braced footnotes with an anchor “[1]” (“[2]” for a second in one paragraph) at the citing word, absorbing the space or line break before it, and placed the note after its paragraph as “[Footnote n: …]”, dropping the transcription's “1.” note label; joined wrapped prose lines with single spaces; chapter numbers became level-2 headings with the chapter title as a level-3 heading, and the prefatory extract and appendix titles became level-2 headings. Underscore emphasis kept as in the file. Sixty-three readings in blocks 18–166 were then corrected to the 1883 Osgood printing after collation (see edition). A further 102 places in blocks 9–645 were corrected after the Grade 11 school-night passages were collated and every collated passage was rechecked for word division (see edition); scope.collated records the collated ranges.
